cases.expected: The production counter source records occupied slots, retained peaks, minimum free space, attributed failures and stack paint boundaries.
cases.recovery: Released slots return current occupancy to zero while peaks, failures and stack saturation stay latched.

cases.expected: Fresh processes complete the trap, leaf and output-length matrix with unsaturated capacity snapshots.
cases.recovery: The shell answers after the quiet interval and a final successful snapshot.

cases.expected: Twelve streams spill beyond the static libc pool without a kernel file-table failure.
cases.recovery: Every stream closes and a subsequent open succeeds.

cases.expected: A bounded cooperating workload attributes refusal to the process table and increments only the process failure counter.
cases.recovery: Every child exits and is reaped before a subsequent creation succeeds.

cases.expected: Distinct live in-core inode identities fill the table and increment only the inode failure counter.
cases.recovery: Released identities permit a subsequent iget allocation.

cases.expected: Cooperating holders reach the system table rather than one process descriptor limit and increment only the file failure counter.
cases.recovery: Closing holders permits a subsequent falloc allocation.

cases.expected: putc and b_to_q refuse at the aligned pool boundary with the intended failure accounting.
cases.recovery: Draining whole blocks preserves byte order and permits retry.

cases.expected: A deterministic seam distinguishes B_BUSY occupancy from delayed writes and increments pressure when all buffers are busy.
cases.recovery: A released buffer completes the waiter and dirty data reaches the modeled device.

cases.expected: NCARGS, cross-block replay, SwapRAM migration and raw-swap fallback preserve the serialized argument stream.
cases.recovery: Every success and injected failure releases the extent and codec workspace.

cases.expected: The signal fixture reports its success marker, zero status, aligned frame and preserved registers.
cases.recovery: The interrupted path returns and a subsequent capacity snapshot succeeds.

cases.expected: Separate child reads fault for kernel, peripheral and flash regions while the allowed user-window control succeeds.
cases.recovery: The parent and shell survive every child fault and residue clearing receives an independent verdict.

cases.expected: Patterned data, stack and u-area bytes survive SwapRAM evacuation to raw swap.
cases.recovery: Every child returns with its pattern intact and the pool accepts later work.

cases.expected: SMALL to LARGE to SMALL transitions preserve patterned children across every epoch.
cases.recovery: The final SMALL process runs after the LARGE image releases its window.

cases.expected: The accepted LARGE image restores after fork and the oversized image receives the declared refusal.
cases.recovery: A bounded ordinary image executes after the refusal.

cases.expected: The extracted production loop exchanges all 3072 bytes and stops at the exact end pointers.
cases.recovery: A second exchange restores both patterned regions.

cases.expected: Parallel find, du and tar complete with checksums, synchronized storage and zero unexpected capacity failures.
cases.recovery: Reboot, fsck, free-block accounting and a final shell command succeed.

cases.expected: A bounded terminal workload fills the physical clist pool and attributes refusal to the clist counter.
cases.recovery: Draining the queue preserves byte order and a subsequent terminal write succeeds.

cases.expected: A bounded workload holds every buffer busy, attributes the wait to buffer pressure and preserves delayed-write data.
cases.recovery: Releasing one buffer wakes the waiter, completes writeback and permits a subsequent allocation.

cases.expected: Separate child reads fault for protected kernel, peripheral and flash regions while the allowed user-window control succeeds on silicon.
cases.recovery: The parent and shell survive every child fault and a subsequent capacity snapshot succeeds.

cases.expected: Distinct u-area patterns survive repeated silicon context switches across the complete configured exchange extent.
cases.recovery: Every switched process resumes with its own pattern and the final shell command succeeds.

cases.recovery: Every child exits and is reaped before a subsequent creation succeeds.

cases.recovery: Released identities permit a subsequent iget allocation.

cases.expected: Cooperating holders fill the emulated system file table and increment only the file failure counter.
cases.recovery: Closing holders permits a subsequent falloc allocation.

cases.expected: Emulated terminal traffic fills the clist pool and attributes refusal to the clist counter.
cases.recovery: Draining the queue preserves byte order and permits a subsequent terminal write.

cases.expected: An emulated workload holds every buffer busy, attributes the wait and preserves delayed-write data.
cases.recovery: Releasing one buffer wakes the waiter, completes writeback and permits a subsequent allocation.

cases.expected: The bounded emulator workload drives signal, fault, SwapRAM and context-switch paths while sampling the complete u-area geometry.

decisions.reserve_rule: Require the full corpus, attributed process exhaustion, successful reap and subsequent creation, plus Renode and board receipts before any decrement.
Require an explicit positive reserve above the greatest admitted peak, distinct in-core exhaustion and release/reallocation recovery.
Require system-table attribution distinct from a per-process descriptor refusal, close/reopen recovery and a positive reserve.
Require putc and b_to_q exhaustion, byte-order recovery, bounded physical terminal traffic and a positive measured reserve.
Preserve exec-spool and packed-decoder lifetimes; require all-busy attribution, delayed-write recovery and zero unexpected waits in Renode and board runs.
Require signal, interrupt, deliberate-fault, SwapRAM and context-switch coverage, stack/frame analysis, exchange geometry and separate Renode and silicon receipts.
